alerts.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 12 at 3:15PM PDT until August 12 at 6:15PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
alerts.description:
FFWREV

The National Weather Service in Reno has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Storey County in western Nevada...
South Central Washoe County in western Nevada...

* Until 615 PM PDT.

* At 315 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Reno, Sparks, Hidden Valley, Damonte Ranch, Lockwood, Reno-Tahoe
International Airport, Mustang.
alerts.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued August 12 at 8:19AM PDT until August 13 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of western Nevada, including the following area,
Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden Area. This includes the Bug and
Stallion Fires.

* WHEN...From 2 PM PDT this afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in rock, mud, and debris
flows in and near active fire perimeters, steep terrain, and poorly
drained urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rain from thunderstorms primarily during the afteroon and
evening hours today and Thursday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 12 at 3:15PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
alerts.description:
At 310 PM PDT, strong thunderstorms continue to develop across the
eastern Sierra and western Nevada. These storms will increase in
coverage northward through the late afternoon.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 40 to 50 mph, up to penny size hail, heavy
rainfall with the potential for flash flooding, and blowing
dust downwind of dry sinks and playas.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible. Heavy rain may cause flash flooding, debris flows
and flooded roads. Blowing dust could lower visibility and
make travel dangerous.

Locations impacted include...
Reno, Carson City, South Lake Tahoe, Fallon, Mammoth Lakes, Chalfant,
Crowley Lake, Sonora Pass, Gardnerville, Virginia City, June Lake,
Pyramid Lake, Lee Vining, Twin Lakes, Lahontan Reservoir, Incline
Village, Toms Place, Bodie, Benton, and Bridgeport.
alerts.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads.
